This Is Supposedly THE Wildest Lamborghini Revuelto Out There
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke
Have you ever looked at the Lamborghini Revuelto and thought that this thing definitely needs to look more aggressive? Probably not, because it already does. After all, we are talking about the Raging Bull’s new-age flagship supercar, so you know it’s been designed to easily stand out in a sea of exotic rides.
However, regardless of whether you think this model needs to tap into its more aggressive side or not, there are plenty of tuners out there that will gladly take your money in return for all kinds of modifications. The list is comprehensive, as it includes pretty much everything, from various body kits to new wheels, aftermarket suspensions, custom interiors where the sky is basically the limit, and the occasional power boost.
Over the years, because production of the Lamborghini Revuelto started in 2023 at Sant’Agata Bolognese in Italy, we have seen numerous modded examples , some of which were quite fine, and others not so much. We won’t point to any of them in this story, because we are not here to do that. Instead, we will star pointing the spotlight to the pictured example. Or, better said, the one shared on video below at the bottom of the page, and in the gallery above.
The reel was shared on Instagram not long ago by @creativebespoke, which claims that this is the “wildest Revuelto on the planet.” We kid you not, that’s what the short caption, which also includes a few other details about this particular build, says, and while we can definitely think of a few other projects that are on the kitschy side of the tuning game (ahem, Mansory!), this one does not seem to be that controversial.
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke Nevertheless, it is definitely wacky, as this Lamborghini Revuelto features quite a few modifications. These include a widebody kit said to have been signed by Zacoe Performance . And now you know why this supercar looks familiar, don’t you? The front fender and rear three-quarter panel attachments have thus come from the quoted tuner’s portfolio, just like the new front hood, the side skirts, the roof scoop, and a few other things.
The front bumper looks like the OEM piece to us, but it does feature what seems to be a more pronounced apron. Things get even crazier at the rear due to the new diffuser, which four huge extra lights integrated into the fins. These stretch all the from the standard taillights to the lower part of the supercar. And if that wasn’t enough, then you should also know that this machine has an extra brake light in the middle of the diffuser, for a motorsport-like vibe, and a large wing resting on the rear deck.
Creative Bespoke says that the wheels are also on the custom side of things, as if that wasn’t evident from the reel shared below, and these were signed by MV Forged. Unfortunately, we cannot tell you what they’re called, as this information hasn’t been released, nor how big they are. What we can reveal is that the rear ones are a lot wider than the front ones, and they feature a V-spoke pattern. The Balloon White paint protection film will keep the body safe from the usual chips and scratches.
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke Don’t go anywhere yet, because we also have to mention the custom interior. The cockpit’s new upholstery is said to have been handcrafted, and was the work of @cb_autosalon. That’s what @creativebespoke says, anyway, and guess what? We haven’t seen it. That’s because the clip showing this Lamborghini Revuelto does not offer a single glimpse inside the Italian supercar. Thus, we cannot talk about the materials used, the colors, and other work that might have gone into it.
Last but not least, the supercar in question is said to have a “race exhaust system.” Thus, it is definitely more sonorous, though you will not hear it in the clip, because Creative Bespoke chose some background music instead over the V12 burble. We could also be looking at a few extra horses, but the difference is insignificant to alter the supercar’s performance.
Therefore, we will remind you that the Lamborghini Revuelto needs just 2.5 seconds to complete the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) sprint with no outside intervention. It has a top speed of 217 mph (350 kph), and unlocks 1,001 hp (1,015 ps/747 kW) in total from its plug-in hybrid powertrain.
The same electrified 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12 also powers the more track-focused, quicker, rarer, and pricier SuperVeloce. The Lamborghini Revuelto SV premiered earlier this year, boasting 1,050 hp (1,065 ps/783 kW) combined, and needing 2.4 seconds to sprint to 62 mph. The top speed in this case is, however, a bit lower, at 216 mph (348 kph).
Now, if you happened to own a Lamborghini Revuelto and were looking to have it tuned, would you have opted for this makeover? That would be a no for me, because the stock supercar simply looks a lot better in my eyes. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Creative Bespoke International (@creativebespoke)
